questions.stem: An odd residue a modulo 128 is called an odd-square residue if some odd integer x satisfies x²≡a (mod128). Without listing all 128 possibilities, classify a=9,13,17,21,33,49. Name the exact defining criterion and give one counterexample to 'all odd residues work'.
conditions: All six candidate residues are odd.
Classification, not finding individual square roots, is the primary requested answer.

answer.summary: Yes:9,17,33,49. No:13,21. Criterion for k>=3: odd a≡1 mod8.
reasoning: For necessity, (2t+1)^2=4t(t+1)+1≡1 mod8. For sufficiency, modulo8 every residue 1 mod8 has a root; if x²≡a modulo2^k, replacing odd x by x+2^(k−1) flips the k-th binary bit of the square modulo2^(k+1) (k>=3), allowing a lift to either residue. Hence induction.
9,17,33,49 have residue1 modulo8; 13 and21 have residue5 modulo8.
The counterexample5 modulo8 proves oddness alone does not suffice.
